title: Easier way to run apps on the dedicated GPU
line: On computers with a dedicated graphics card, right-clicking an app in Kickoff, Kicker, search results or the Task Manager now offers to run it on that card.
explanation: Running an app on the dedicated GPU was only possible by setting PrefersNonDefaultGPU ("Run using dedicated graphics card") in Edit Application or the file properties, so it applied to every launch and was hard to find; no launcher offered it as a one-off. KIO had the GPU detection (switcheroo-control, or PowerDevil as a fallback) and the matching environment, but kept both private. KIO's ApplicationLauncherJob now has a RunOnDiscreteGpu run flag (applies the discrete GPU's environment and skips D-Bus activation, which can't carry it) and a public hasDiscreteGpu(). Kickoff/Kicker (app entries, favorites, search results, recent apps) show "Run Using Dedicated Graphics Card" and the Task Manager shows "Run Using…" on launchers and "Open New Window Using Dedicated Graphics Card" on tasks that can open a new window, only when a dedicated GPU exists and the app doesn't already prefer it.

commits.message:
ApplicationLauncherJob: add RunOnDiscreteGpu run flag

Launchers could only start an app on the discrete GPU when its desktop
file sets PrefersNonDefaultGPU, so there was no way to do it just once.
The new flag and hasDiscreteGpu() let them offer a one-off action.

BUG: 392523

applets/kicker: add "Run Using Dedicated Graphics Card" action

Starting an app on the dedicated GPU needed editing its desktop entry
first. On systems with one, the app context menu in Kickoff, Kicker and
search results now has an action that runs it there just this once.

BUG: 392523

applets/taskmanager: offer to run apps on the dedicated graphics card

Starting an app on the dedicated GPU needed editing its desktop entry
first. On systems with one, the context menu of launchers and of tasks
that can open a new window now has an action to do it just this once.

BUG: 392523
